beats.narration: Checkpoint five: four deployment scenarios, each needing a transport and a scope. Pause here if you haven't made your picks.

elements.text: ⏸ pick transport + scope for all four first

beats.narration: One: a local SQLite query tool, used only on your machine. Stdio, local scope. It's a subprocess with an audience of one. Two: a code search service on company infrastructure, for the whole engineering team. HTTP, project scope: it's remote, so stdio physically can't reach it, and committing the config shares it with every clone. Three: an experimental scraper you're testing this week. Either transport works, but the scope is local, because project scope would commit your experiment to everyone. And four: the security scanner IT wants on every developer's installation. HTTP, enterprise scope: pushed through managed settings, not left to individual developers. The two classic misses: stdio pointed at a remote server, which can't work because stdio spawns locally. And project scope on an experiment, which ships your test to the whole team.

elements.text: ✗ stdio → remote server: a subprocess can't cross the network
✗ project scope on experiments: commits your test to the team

beats.narration: Same two questions, every time: where does the server run, and who needs it? Answer those and the config writes itself. Next section: enterprise integration.

elements.text:
where does it run? who needs it?
→ the config writes itself
